newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Extraordinary gains to boost Benguet net.
newsitem.headline: Extraordinary gains to boost Benguet net.

text.p: Philippines' Benguet Corp said on Friday it expected better income in the second half of the year, after posting a net loss of 73.1 million pesos in the first six months.

"Payments of additional option money for the Kingking Project and from the sale of the Paracale plant facilities were received in July and August 1996 and should positively influence third quarter 1996 results," Benguet president Dennis Belmonte said in a statement.
The company received early this month 97.8 million pesos from Base Metals Mineral Resources Corp for the sale of its Paracale mine.
It also received $10 million from Echo Bay Mines Ltd and TVI Pacific Inc last July for the right to explore its Kingking copper and gold mine.
Belmonte said the company is on the lookout for other joint venture partners for its gold operation.

"Offers for joint venture operation of the Benguet mine received from certain parties are being evaluated. The Benguet mine is in the market for potential investors either on outright sale or joint venture agreement," the statement said. However, Belmonte said a series of natural calamities might dampen its bottomline. Benguet mines have suffered from lower production and higher expenses because of these.
The higher grade ore deposit of its Antamok open pit gold mine in northern Philippines was recently covered by a landslide, thereby cutting down its gold production output.
"The situation was further worsened by a slide at the open pit on July 26, 1996 caused by typhoon Gloria which damaged the mill water supply line," Belmonte said.
Its Dizon mine sustained cracks in its open pit wall during an earthquake on July 31.
"Compounded by strong rains that brought record amount of water, slides have occured at some portions of the pit," he added.
At present, the country's oldest mining corporation is planning to convert some of its mines into other industrial uses.

"We are currently studying the possibility of converting the use of our vast landholdings from an industry traditionally perceived as unfriendly to the envirnoment to one that is environmentally supportive and serving the people in another way," Belmonte said.
"Should the studies prove positive, Benguet could well be entering a new industry as it moves on to its centennial year."
Benguet extracts gold, copper concentrates and chromite.
